page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 architecture, utilizing the Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps. The CPU architecture includes hardware-accelerated AES cryptography but lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512, or AMX.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8gb.16xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark physics tests all register in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 7387.52 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 466.21 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. Additionally, while LLM text generation for medium and large models is strong, text generation for small 135M models is poor, indicating specific architectural constraints for certain lightweight sequential workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64-based Graviton architecture offers high compute density and memory throughput per resource unit compared to traditional x86 architectures, making it highly efficient for highly parallelized workloads. The instance is well-suited for high-throughput database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing. Conversely, workloads requiring local NVMe storage, GPU acceleration, or x86 vector instructions are not compatible with this hardware profile.
